prompt: Three blank rectangular paper cards drifting on the open sea, carried along by the current in a loose trailing line, physically floating in the water like small paper rafts, seen from slightly above at a low angle, in perspective, so that each card appears as a foreshortened slanted quadrilateral lying on the water surface, never facing the viewer, never upright, never flat like a sticker. The three cards trail one after another from the far upper right towards the centre of the image, far apart, never touching, never overlapping: the farthest one small in the upper right, the middle one larger, the nearest one the largest, close to the centre and about a quarter of the image width. Each card is turned at its own angle and gently tilted by the swell; on each card one corner or short edge dips slightly under the water and is wet and darker, while the rest of the card rides dry on the surface. Each card is a stiff landscape print, about 3:2, wider than tall: an off-white #fbfcfd mount with a thin ink grey outline and, inside it, one large empty panel bounded by a thin crisp ink grey line. The panel is completely blank, one plain uniform flat light off-white tone, nothing drawn inside it, no picture, no pattern, no hatching, no shading, and it stays fully visible, the water only touching the outer edge of the mount. The nearest, largest card has a thick bold rim of saturated violet #7C5CD6 all around its mount; the other two cards have plain off-white rims. The cards are drawn in crisp off-white and ink grey line art with fine engraved shading on their thin edges. The water reacts to every card: a thin off-white foam line where the card meets the water, small engraved ripples spreading from its edges, a short narrow wake of fine curved lines trailing behind it towards the upper right showing the direction of the current, and a soft darker reflection drawn in denser line hatching just below it. Long gentle current lines flow across the sea from the upper right towards the centre, following the path of the cards. Richly detailed engraved nautical chart style, like a fine antique sea chart printed in two inks: the sea built from many layers of fine wave lines and hatching, line density increasing towards the deep water to give depth, tonal bands from deep cerulean at the bottom to lighter cerulean at the top, bathymetric contour lines with small depth soundings drawn as tiny dots, subtle foam strokes and a few glints of light on the crests. Every wave is drawn as visible engraved line work, like a steel engraving, never painted, never smooth. Crisp sharp lines of several weights, intricate but calm, premium print quality, high detail, elegant. No photographic rendering, no glow, no gradient, no text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark, water filling the whole image edge to edge, the cards in the upper two thirds from the centre to the right, open calm water on the left third and along the bottom. Palette strictly limited to medium cerulean ocean blue #0072a8 and its tints and shades, off-white #fbfcfd, ink grey #13212b and saturated violet #7C5CD6 on the rim of the nearest card only.
